title: QRD headings, in order
text: Every heading of the QRD template appears with its exact wording and in the template order. Optional headings may be left out.
simplified: Alternative wording in angle brackets in the template is accepted as written in the app (for example "<and other handling>").

title: Required sections are filled
text: Each required section has content. If a section does not apply, the template usually gives the wording to use instead (for example "Not applicable.").

title: Black triangle for additional monitoring
text: A medicine under additional monitoring carries the black inverted triangle and the standard statement at the start of the SmPC and the package leaflet. Medicines not under additional monitoring do not.

title: Reporting statement in 4.8
text: Section 4.8 ends with the standard text on reporting suspected adverse reactions, pointing to the national reporting system listed in Appendix V.

title: Frequency categories in 4.8
text: Adverse reactions are listed by MedDRA system organ class and frequency, using the convention very common (≥1/10), common (≥1/100 to <1/10), uncommon (≥1/1,000 to <1/100), rare (≥1/10,000 to <1/1,000), very rare (<1/10,000) and not known. Words such as "frequent" or "occasional" are not used.
simplified: The app looks for the category names and for non-standard frequency words; it does not check the system organ class order.

title: Excipients with a known effect
text: Excipients listed in the annex to the excipients guideline need the set statement in the package leaflet (section 2) and the matching information in SmPC section 4.4; most must also be named on the outer carton.
simplified: The app knows six common excipients and checks for the key words of each statement, not the full text or the dose thresholds.

title: Standard statements in the leaflet
text: The leaflet starts with the "Read all of this leaflet carefully" box, section 4 ends with "Reporting of side effects" pointing to Appendix V, and the last line gives the date it was last revised.

title: Leaflet consistent with the SmPC
text: The leaflet says the same things as the SmPC in patient language: contraindications in 4.3 appear under "Do not take", strengths match, and the warnings in 4.4 are reflected in "Warnings and precautions".
simplified: The app compares strengths and checks that an allergy contraindication in 4.3 is mirrored in the leaflet.

title: Keep out of the sight and reach of children
text: Section 6 of the outer packaging carries exactly "Keep out of the sight and reach of children."

title: Name in Braille
text: The name of the medicinal product is in Braille on the packaging; where there are several strengths, the strength is included. The text to be embossed is given in section 16.
simplified: The app checks the text given for Braille, not the embossing itself.

title: Safety features
text: Prescription medicines carry a unique identifier in a 2D data matrix and an anti-tampering device. Section 17 states "2D barcode carrying the unique identifier included." and section 18 shows the human-readable product code (PC), serial number (SN) and, where applicable, national reimbursement number (NN).
simplified: The app checks the template statements and the PC/SN/NN lines, not a real code.

title: Annex II conditions
text: Annex II names the manufacturer responsible for batch release, gives the legal status for supply in B (for example "Medicinal product subject to medical prescription."), and carries the standard statements on periodic safety update reports (the EURD list, Article 107c(7) of Directive 2001/83/EC) in C and on the risk management plan (Module 1.8.2, when an updated RMP is due) in D.
simplified: The app checks the supply statement and the key phrases of the PSUR and RMP statements, not every word; conditions specific to a product (additional risk minimisation, post-authorisation measures) are not checked.

title: Immediate packaging particulars
text: Blisters, strips and small immediate packaging give the expiry date after "EXP" and the batch number after "Lot". Small units also give the route of administration with the name, the method of administration and the contents by weight, volume or unit.
at: QRD template v10.4, Annex IIIA; Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 55
simplified: The app checks the prefixes and that the route and contents are given; the date and batch are printed on the packaging line.

title: Generic SmPC matches the reference
text: The SmPC of a generic medicinal product follows the reference SmPC. Differences are expected only where the products differ (strengths offered, composition, appearance and excipients in sections 1 to 3 and 6, and the holder, numbers and dates in sections 7 to 10), and in parts left out because they refer to indications or dosage forms still covered by patent law.
simplified: The app compares section by section after swapping the product and company names; national authorities also accept differences that the app cannot judge, which you would waive with a reason.

title: Patent-protected indication fully left out
text: When an indication still covered by patent law is left out of a generic SmPC, every mention that depends on it goes too: indication, posology, adverse reaction data and clinical data.
simplified: Mentions are found by keywords defined for the left-out indication in the exercise.

title: Particulars agree with the SmPC
text: The name, strength, pharmaceutical form, pack size, authorisation number and holder on the packaging agree with the SmPC.

title: Blue box for national particulars
text: Centrally authorised products may carry a "blue box" on the outer packaging for national particulars (for example price or reimbursement) required by a member state.
simplified: Shown as a hint only: whether a blue box is needed depends on the member states where the pack is sold.

title: QR codes need agency assessment
text: A QR code or other mobile-scanning link in the labelling or leaflet of a centrally authorised product must be submitted to EMA, and the content it links to must be consistent with the approved product information and not promotional.

title: Revision dates
text: SmPC section 10 gives the date of revision, and the leaflet ends with the month and year it was last revised.
at: QRD template v10.4, SmPC section 10 and Annex IIIB

title: Strengths agree
text: The strengths in the SmPC name and composition agree with the product and with the labelling.

title: Plain language in the leaflet
text: The leaflet should be easy to read: short sentences, everyday words, explained medical terms.
simplified: Reading grade is an estimate (Flesch-Kincaid style) shown as a hint.

title: User test passed
text: The leaflet is user tested (or bridged to a tested leaflet). The usual success standard: for each question, at least 16 of 20 participants (about 81%) find the information and show they understand it, over two rounds of 10 on the final text.
simplified: The simulator estimates participants' results from the leaflet text; a real test uses real people.

title: Approved terms in the translation
text: A translation uses the approved terms from the term base for each source term it translates.

title: Numbers kept in the translation
text: Every number in a section of the source (doses, durations, strengths) appears in the matching section of the translation.
simplified: The app compares digits section by section.

title: Every section translated
text: Every section of the source has a translated section with content.

title: No promotional wording
text: Product information must not be promotional. Words such as "best", "safest" or "superior" do not belong in it.
